source_text:
<Προοίμιον> Κατὰ λόγον ἢ νόμον ἢ εἱμαρμένην ἢ τύχην αἱ τῶν πραγμάτων
ἐκβάσεις, ἐπιγοναὶ καὶ φθοραί, ἀλλοιώσεις καὶ ἰάματ<α>· ὧν ἕκαστον καλὸν εἰδέναι,
συναγαγόντας ἐκ πάντων ὠφέλειαν ποικίλην καρπουμένην, θεραπείαν παθῶν ἢ
ἱστορίαν ἀπόρρητον ἢ λόγου κάλλος· ἅπερ ἔν τε τοῖς φθάνουσι καὶ τοῖς ἑπομένοις,
ὥς γε οἶμαι, κατὰ τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ μέτριον κατώρθωται.
pass_a_gloss: Proem. According-to reason or law or fate or chance the outcomes of affairs, births and destructions, alterations and healings; of-which each is good to-know, gathering from all a varied profit bearing-fruit, therapy of passions or hidden history or beauty of speech; which-things in both the preceding and the following, as I think, according-to my own modest-measure has-been-achieved.
pass_b_english: Proem. The issues of affairs — births and destructions, alterations and healings — come by reason, or by law, or by fate, or by chance. It is good to know each of these, gathering from them all a varied profit that bears fruit: a therapy of sufferings, or a hidden history, or beauty of speech. These things, in what has gone before and in what follows, have been achieved, as I think, according to my own modest measure.
